subject: tile guard belongs in YOUR module: $a2ec/$a2f0
body:
`tile` (discr-qcb) has landed and flagged that tile::damage has no guard for a
hit on an already-destroyed cell. It transcribed $a31c-$a354 literally and did
not invent one, which was correct -- because the guard is in YOUR code path,
not theirs. From the disassembly:

    $a2ec  tst.w ($00,a0,d5.w)   ; the cell's TYPE word (+$00)
    $a2f0  beq.w $a3ea           ; type == 0 -> skip, never reaches the damage
    $a300  tst.w ($00,a0,d5.w)   ; same test on the other path
    $a304  beq.w $a3ea

So before disc::step calls tile::damage, gate on Tile::walkable() (type != 0).
A destroyed cell is skipped entirely -- no second TileDestroyed event.

Second thing in the same window, which affects the damage value you pass:

    $a30c  move.w ($02,a0,d5.w),d6   ; hp
    $a310  sub.w  ($0016,a5),d6      ; hp -= disc damage
    $a314  cmp.w  #$0001,$00006d9a
    $a31a  bne.b  $a32e
    $a31c  sub.w  ($0016,a5),d6      ; ...subtracted AGAIN when $6d9a == 1

$6d9a is a damage multiplier: the disc's damage is applied once normally and
twice when $6d9a == 1, and $a32e tests it against 3 for a further path. Its
semantics are NOT decoded -- I have filed a bead. Do not model the multiplier;
pass the disc's +$16 damage once and leave a comment citing $a314 and the
bead. Single application is the base case, so the golden fixture should still
match unless $6d9a is 1 in it.

        in wt/player (15 tests, 11 of them new).

Implemented: states 1 ($f5e2 walk left) and 2 ($f7f6 walk right) only --
facing ($6ca9), X step +/-3 ($f658/$f86c) with the +/-24 destination probe
and the tile type-word walkability gate ($f63e/$f852), and the $6cb0 grid
cell = column(X via $7bfe) + 8 + (4 if Y > 14). The four measured samples
(117/18->15, 152/18->16, 8/18->13, 117/2->11) are unit tests, as are the
movement bounds. Every other jump-table entry is an opaque pass-through and
moves no field: 5,11,14,19,20,21,23,24,27,31 marked "UNKNOWN: see bd
discr-75o", 16/17 "UNKNOWN: see bd discr-rf9". No change requested to
docs/state-schema.md; nothing outside player.rs touched.

ONE PLACE WHERE I READ THE NOTES AGAINST THEMSELVES -- please sanity-check.

docs/disc-notes.md says the walk is "probed +/-24 ahead and range-checked
against 8 and $98", and reports/findings.md shows the range check branching
to $f644/$f85c, the same "no cell" path an unwalkable destination takes. Read
as a movement stop, that would floor the walk at X = 32 and cap it at 128 --
24 units short of each wall. But Part 4 measured the Left run reaching
exactly 8 and the Right run exactly 152, and from idle X = 117 neither is
117 +/- 3n (150 + 3 = 153; 9 - 3 = 6). So the ST must clamp X into 8..152,
and the +/-24 range check cannot be what stops the walk -- it reads as a
guard keeping the index inside the $7bfe table's 145-byte domain.

So I modelled it as: probe index clamped into 8..152, the tile type word is
the only thing that blocks a step, and X = (X +/- 3).clamp(8, 152). That
reproduces every measured value. What I could NOT settle from the notes is
what the blocked flag (d2, st.b at $f64e/$f862) is actually consumed by --
$f7b8/$f9ce are unexplored. If someone disassembles those and it turns out
the flag does gate the write, this is the line to revisit; it is documented
in the doc comment on walk(). Say the word and I will file it as a bead.

Also not modelled, by design and per discr-75o: transitions INTO states 1/2.
The notes give a handler per state number but nothing that selects the next
one, so state_index is an input to player::step, never an output. A caller
driving only Input will therefore never walk -- if I7 integration expects
otherwise, that is the gap.

1. tracecheck --skip-waived. It halted on players[1].world_x at frame 1 of every
   trace: the schema marked players[1].* compared while p2 AI is waived
   (discr-b6x) and the trace has no $6c59 column, so a waiver was being reported
   as a divergence and every number worth having was hidden behind it.
   --skip-waived resyncs the schema's waived rows from the trace each tick
   instead of comparing them. Default UNCHANGED; both modes print which is in
   force. First divergence with it: frame 11, players[0].state_index 20 vs 0,
   10 ticks matched, owned by discr-75o.

2. Field table reconciled. players[1].* -> waived:discr-b6x, and the four
   unknowns found during wave 2 added as waived behaviour rows (discr-tan,
   discr-217, discr-5w5, discr-z8m). Totals are now 15 compared / 12 waived /
   6 excluded and tracecheck's header prints the same three numbers, so a drift
   between tool and file shows up on every run. The stale "+$04 vs +$06" open
   question at the foot of the file is replaced by its Part 9 resolution.

3. make core-check = fmt + clippy -D warnings + test + tracecheck on the golden
   fixture with --min-agree 10. It gates on the LENGTH of the matching prefix,
   not on the run being clean, because the divergence is bead-owned and a gate
   that is red by design gets ignored. Same flag name and reasoning as
   scripts/oracle_diff.py's --min-agree. 10 lives in the Makefile as
   TRACE_MIN_AGREE with the reason next to it. `make tracecheck` is the ungated
   view (exits 1). Oracle targets untouched; disc-app still out of
   default-members; no new system dependency.

TWO THINGS FOR YOU, BOTH IN disc-core, NEITHER FIXED BY ME

discr-xfw (P1) -- player+$09 is almost certainly NOT a 1/2 facing flag.
  disc-core and the notes read $6ca9 as 1 = left ($f5e2), 2 = right ($f7f6).
  The golden fixture says otherwise: p1's +$09 takes {0,1,11,20,23} and p2's
  takes {0,1,2,15,16,18,20} -- exactly the sets their state_index takes, ONE
  FRAME BEHIND. facing[n] == state[n-1] holds on 96 of 99 p1 frame pairs; all
  three exceptions are +$09 = 11 against a sampled +$0e of 0.
  So +$09 looks like the previous state, written at handler entry, and the 1/2
  reading is indistinguishable from it on states 1 and 2 alone -- which is all
  the notes had. disc-core's Player::facing is therefore passing for the wrong
  reason wherever it passes. That is a disc-core field name and a disc-core
  write in player::walk, so it is yours to route, not mine to change.
  Reproduce: tracecheck ... --skip-waived --resync 'players[0].state_index'
             -> frame 12, players[0].facing, expected 20, got 0

discr-0fm (P1) -- disc world_z is not always +1 per frame.

body:
The flight cycle from Part 9 is implemented and committed.

  branch: agent/disc
  SHA:    af37324b8edd6277575f36867b254051d3a21ed5
  file:   crates/disc-core/src/disc.rs (only file touched)
  gates:  cargo fmt / clippy --all-targets -D warnings / cargo test (43) /
          make core-check -- all green

WHAT LANDED

  world_z += dir_kind, bounded by Z_NEAR = 0 and Z_FAR = 54.
  * near bound clamps and writes dir_kind = +1 (disc 0 f70 steps 2 -> 0;
    disc 1 does the same at f208 -- two discs, so mirrored, not modelled);
  * the far turn costs one step, 54 -> 53 (f52 and f152, and golden f52);
  * dwell at Z_FAR: world_z >= 54 with dir_kind > 0 returns early, so the
    WHOLE record holds -- world_x included, vel_x 1 and all.

  Nothing carries a MODELLED marker: every arm above appears at least twice
  in the fixture. The pre-existing MODELLED note on the world_x floor/flip
  is untouched.

THE DWELL DURATION -- what I chose and why

  Kept as a state the record can be in, entered by step() and never left by
  it: the disc stays frozen until something writes a negative dir_kind. I did
  not hard-code 17 and I did not derive the timing. Documented on Z_FAR as
  // UNKNOWN: see bd discr-0fm.

  RETURN_DIR_KIND = -3 is a new pub const, and worth flagging: the turn is
  NOT neg.w of +1. The magnitude changes 1 -> 3 across it, so $a606 alone
  does not account for the flip and something else writes the kind. reflect()
  still transcribes neg.w literally and is now visibly narrower than what the
  fixture does.

MEASUREMENTS (before -> after)

  tile_damage --skip-waived                      22 -> 22 ticks
      first divergence unchanged: f23 discs[0].world_y (discr-tan)
  tile_damage --skip-waived --resync world_y     33 -> 33 ticks
      first divergence unchanged: f34 discs[0].world_x, expected 45 got 46
  golden --skip-waived                           10 -> 10 ticks
      f11 players[0].state_index (discr-75o) -- no regression

  The official numbers did not move, and the reason is one frame short of my
  work: f34 is the unexplained vel_x decay 2 -> 1, which lands the frame
  BEFORE the dwell starts. It is a world_x/vel_x row, owner discr-217 /
  discr-b6x, not a world_z row. So the comparison did NOT reach a tile event
  (the nearest is f70).

  The z work is real, though, and measurable with the x row resynced to its
  owning bead:

    --resync discs[0].world_y --resync discs[0].vel_x --resync discs[0].world_x
        34 -> 51 ticks
        first divergence f52 discs[0].world_z, expected 53 got 54

  i.e. the outbound leg and the entire 17-frame dwell now replay exactly, and
  the run stops precisely at the undecoded dwell exit (discr-0fm). That is the
  honest measure of this change.

TWO FINDINGS FOR WHOEVER OWNS discr-0fm AND discr-b6x

1. A LEAD ON THE DWELL EXIT, n=2, deliberately NOT modelled.
   Both dwell exits (f52, f152) are the exact frame player 2 enters
   state_index 17. So is f190 -- and at f190 disc slot 1 appears from nothing
   at wz 53 with dir_kind -3 and vel_x 4. State 17 reads as "the opponent
   plays the disc", and the dwell as the disc waiting at the far end to be
   played. Three occurrences of state 17, two of them dwell exits, the third
   a serve with no disc dwelling. I left it out of step(): n=2, and it would
   couple disc flight to the player state machine on a correlation. But if
   someone wants the fixture to replay past f52, that is the lever -- and
   players[1].* is already resynced by tracecheck, so it would work.

2. STEERING IS NOT UNIFORMLY GATED OFF, and the two aim variants are BOTH
   live in one fixture. Relevant to discr-217/discr-b6x, contradicts the
   current note that the block never runs:
   * f12..f34 fit $a816 exactly: target = p2.x - $13. f34 is the at-target
     decay -- p2.x = 63, target 44, disc at 44, vel 2 -> 1. That IS the
     unexplained decay, and $a722 explains it.
   * f99..f124 fit $a7d8 exactly: target = p2.x - 4 = 52. The whole
     48 -> 54 -> 50 hunt is the rule, checked frame by frame.
   * f1..f11 fit NEITHER (vel pinned at -2 with the target far above).
   So the gate is not a global off switch and the offset selection changes
   within a single run. I did not touch steer() or wire it into step().

3. Minor, for the ceiling question: disc 1 flies at vel_x 4 and DOES clamp
   near the top -- f206 wx 153, f207 wx 155 with vel_x flipping +4 -> -4.
   Disc 0 never gets there. So there may be an upper world_x bound around
   155 for fast discs; nothing to model yet, but "no ceiling" may be a
   statement about disc 0's range rather than about world_x.
